title: Deprecation & Sunset - Pricing & Packaging
transcript:
Head of Product: Alright, let's dive into our plans for the phasing out of the legacy product.

Sales Lead: I've been getting queries from clients about the future of this platform. They're concerned about the potential impact on their operations.

Finance Analyst: I agree. We need to address their concerns while minimizing any financial risk to us.

Customer Success: Speaking of that, I'm worried about the strain on our team if we go for an immediate migration.

Head of Product: I understand that. Let's consider a hybrid approach then, shall we? Deprecate the legacy product while offering selective discounts for migrating users.

Sales Lead: (pauses) That could potentially signal weakness in our pricing strategy, though.

Head of Product: Fair point. But we can position it as a one-time gesture to support our long-term relationships with valued clients.

Sales Lead: I'm still not completely on board, but let's weigh the pros and cons.

Finance Analyst: Alright, let's compare it to the other options. Aggressive deprecation with no discounts would result in substantial revenue loss and potential customer backlash.

Customer Success: Gradual deprecation over 2 years with full maintenance costs is also a no-go. It mitigates revenue loss but may not address customer concerns effectively.

Finance Analyst: And immediate deprecation with full migration assistance would potentially strain our already understaffed team.

Head of Product: Exactly. So, a hybrid approach offers immediate cost savings through deprecation while providing incentives for users to migrate smoothly.

Customer Success: Partial migration assistance and discounts allow customers to transition at their own pace while minimizing our team's workload.

Finance Analyst: But we need to monitor the financial implications of user migrations closely.

Head of Product: Agreed. And we might also need additional support from IT to ensure a smooth migration.

Sales Lead: (sighs) I suppose I can live with it, but I'll need regular updates on the progress and customer feedback.

Customer Success: I'll make sure to keep everyone informed.

Finance Analyst: I'll crunch the numbers and present a detailed analysis of the financial impact.

Head of Product: Excellent. It seems we've reached a decision then. Product Management will own this, and the CEO will sign off.

Sales Lead: Let's make it happen, but remember, we need to stay vigilant and adapt as needed.

Customer Success: Absolutely. I'll ensure our team is prepared for whatever comes our way.

Finance Analyst: I'll start working on the financial analysis right away.

Off-topic Exchange:

Customer Success: (laughs) Ever tried that vegan chili Joe brought in last week?

Finance Analyst: The carnivore in me couldn't stomach it, but surprisingly, it wasn't half bad.

Head of Product: (laughs) Well, at least we agree on something. Now, back to business!

Title: Product Deprecation Decision

Record: In consideration of aggressive deprecation without discounts, it was collectively decided that a hybrid approach offering selective incentives for migrating users would be more favorable, balancing revenue retention with smooth user transitions. This approach also minimizes potential strain on our customer success team. It was noted that additional support from IT may be necessary to ensure a seamless migration. No immediate full migration assistance was proposed due to resource constraints. The team agreed to closely monitor financial implications during the migration process. Further discussion on gradual deprecation, sales concerns, and potential risks were not detailed in this record.
